rules.statement: mul multiplies rs1 by rs2 as XLEN-bit values and writes the lower XLEN bits of the product to the destination register.
mulh, mulhu and mulhsu return the upper XLEN bits of the 2×XLEN-bit product for signed×signed, unsigned×unsigned and signed rs1×unsigned rs2 respectively.

rules.condition: both high and low bits of the same product are required
rules.statement: Use mulh (or mulhu/mulhsu if appropriate) rdh,rs1,rs2 followed by mul rdl,rs1,rs2 to obtain both halves.

rules.condition: using the recommended mulh/mul fusion sequence
rules.statement: Source specifiers rs1 and rs2 must be in the same order in both instructions, and rdh must not be the same as rs1 or rs2.

rules.condition: mulh followed by mul of the same operands
rules.statement: Microarchitectures may fuse the two instructions into a single multiply operation instead of two separate multiplies.
mulw multiplies the lower 32 bits of the source registers and writes the sign extension of the lower 32 bits of the result to the destination register.

rules.condition: RV64 mul used to obtain the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit product
rules.statement: Signed arguments must be proper 32-bit signed values and unsigned arguments must have their upper 32 bits clear.

rules.condition: executing div, divu, rem or remu
rules.statement: div and divu perform XLEN-bit signed and unsigned division of rs1 by rs2 rounding towards zero; rem and remu return the remainder of the corresponding division.
The sign of a nonzero rem result equals the sign of the dividend.

rules.condition: both quotient and remainder are required from the same division
rules.statement: Use div rdq,rs1,rs2 followed by rem rdr,rs1,rs2 (or divu and remu if appropriate).
rdq must not be the same register as rs1 or rs2.

rules.condition: div followed by rem of the same operands
rules.statement: Microarchitectures may fuse the two instructions into a single divide operation instead of two separate divides.
divw and divuw divide the lower 32 bits of rs1 by those of rs2 as signed and unsigned and write the 32-bit quotient sign-extended to 64 bits in rd; remw and remuw give the corresponding remainders.

rules.condition: remw or remuw, including divide by zero
rules.statement: remw and remuw always sign-extend the 32-bit result to 64 bits, including on a divide by zero.
Division by zero returns all bits set (-1 for div/divw, 2^L-1 for divu/divuw) as quotient, and the remainder equals the dividend for rem/remw/remu/remuw.

rules.condition: signed division overflow: most-negative integer divided by -1
rules.statement: On signed overflow the quotient equals the dividend (-2^(L-1)) and the remainder is zero.
Unsigned division overflow does not occur.

rules.condition: language standard mandates divide-by-zero exception causing immediate control flow change
rules.statement: A single branch instruction may be inserted after each divide to implement the required control flow change.
